# Stint limitations

What Stint cannot do, grouped by where you meet it. Each entry says what you see and what still
works, with a link to the page that has the workaround. For every command and setting, see the
[reference](reference.md).

## Requirements and surfaces

### Requirements: Claude Code 2.1.287 and Python 3.9

Stint needs Claude Code 2.1.287 or later and Python 3.9 or later on `PATH` as `python3` or `python`.

**What you see:** without `python3` and without `python` on `PATH`, `stint` does not run. Python
older than 3.9 is not supported.

**What still works:** everything else in Claude Code. See [Reference](reference.md#requirements).

### Where an organization manages Claude Code, Stint's module may not run

Stint's module uses only `session.measure`. That event is not among the ones that Claude Code's
`sec-default` guard keeps from a module of a user-installed plugin (prompt, tool-batch,
session-start and compaction), so the module should run. This is not verified on a machine where an
organization manages Claude Code.

**What you see:** if the guard stops the module, `limits.json` is not written, and without PaceLine
`stint next` waits with `no usage reading yet`.

**What still works:** the queue commands, and with PaceLine the advice, which does not use Stint's
module.

### The Windows power script needs elevation

`scripts/night-power.ps1` sets the Windows Update active hours and the power plan, which needs an
elevated PowerShell for `-Enable` and `-Disable`. It runs on Windows only.

**What you see:** without elevation the script stops with `Active-hours changes need an elevated
PowerShell session. Re-run as Administrator.`

**What still works:** the dry run, which needs no elevation, and, on macOS and Linux, `caffeinate`
and `systemd-inhibit`. See [Keep the computer awake for the
night](how-to.md#keep-the-computer-awake-for-the-night).

## Alongside PaceLine

### PaceLine's leftover pool is gone and its items are not carried over

PaceLine 0.6.0 and earlier had a leftover pool (`paceline queue --pool`) that ran pre-approved items
on the last night before the weekly reset. Stint has no pool: the last part of the week plan already
takes what is left of the week, and the pool needs a fact only PaceLine knows. Stint does not read
PaceLine's pool file.

**What you see:** `stint list` shows no `L` items from the pool, and there is no `--pool` option.

**What still works:** the ordinary queue and its items carry over. Queue the pool's items as
ordinary items in the last night before the weekly reset. See [Move from PaceLine's
queue](how-to.md#move-from-pacelines-queue).

### Two queue copies on a machine with an older PaceLine

PaceLine 0.6.0 and earlier keep their own queue (`paceline queue` and `paceline auto`) in
`state/paceline/night-queue.json`. With such a PaceLine and Stint installed, there are two `queue`
commands. Stint reads PaceLine's file until it writes its own `queue.json`; after its first write
the two queues do not share state. Stint does not detect the other copy.

**What you see:** after Stint's first write, `paceline queue list` and `stint list` show different
queues, and `paceline auto` and `stint next` decide on different ones.

**What still works:** each queue works on its own. Use one of them; a PaceLine that has dropped its
queue ends the overlap. See [Move from PaceLine's queue](how-to.md#move-from-pacelines-queue).

### A run that PaceLine stored without an end ends at 09:00 UTC of its night date

A run stored by PaceLine 0.6.0 or earlier may carry a `night_date` and no `night_end`. Stint ends
such a run at 09:00 UTC of that date, the default start of work. PaceLine used the time zone of its
profile, which Stint does not read.

**What you see:** `stint next` says `night ended` at 09:00 UTC, not at your local start of work.

**What still works:** `stint next --start-run` opens a new run, with the end of tonight's part from
PaceLine, or with none without PaceLine.

## Without PaceLine

### Without PaceLine a run has no end of its own

Without PaceLine there are no working hours to bound a night, so `stint next --start-run` stores a
run with no end. The run closes at its first stop, when the queue is empty or the week stop is
reached: `stint next` stores `ended_at`, and the next `stint next --start-run` opens a new run.

**What you see:** a queue that is left running goes on into the day until its first stop or an empty
queue; `night ended` never appears.

**What still works:** the week stop and the five-hour stop, which apply at every `stint next`. See
[Run without PaceLine](how-to.md#run-without-paceline).

### Several accounts without PaceLine read the latest reading of any session

`limits.json` holds the latest reading of any session on the machine. With two accounts on one
machine, Stint without PaceLine may read the figures of the other account. PaceLine keeps the
accounts apart.

**What you see:** the week and five-hour stops of `stint next` follow figures that may belong to
another account.

**What still works:** with PaceLine, its advice names the account, and Stint stops the run when the
account changes. With one account on the machine, nothing changes.

### Without PaceLine, no open session means no usage reading

Stint reads the limits that Claude Code hands to a session. The module writes them only while a
session measures its limits, and a reading older than 30 minutes is stale.

**What you see:** `stint next` waits with `no usage reading yet` or `usage data stale (<n> min)`.

**What still works:** the queue commands, and the run resumes as soon as a session writes a fresh
reading. See [The queue waits with no usage
reading](troubleshooting.md#the-queue-waits-with-no-usage-reading).

### Without PaceLine there are no model-scoped limits

`stint next` names no model. With PaceLine, `/stint:run` reads each model's own weekly limit from
`paceline status --json`. Without PaceLine no such figures exist, so the agent chooses a model by
the item's needs.

**What you see:** an item may run on a model whose own weekly limit is spent, and fail.

**What still works:** the week and five-hour stops. Defer an item with `stint defer` when it needs a
model that is out of limit.

## The queue

### PaceLine hold calls run under the queue lock

`stint start`, `stint done`, `stint defer` and `stint fail` at the third attempt call PaceLine while
they hold `queue.lock`. A PaceLine call can take up to 60 seconds before Stint gives up, and a
second Stint command waits for the lock for 10 seconds only. A lock is taken over only when it is
older than 300 seconds, so it is never taken from a command that still waits for PaceLine.

**What you see:** while one command waits for PaceLine, another fails with `stint: queue is locked:
<path>`.

**What still works:** the failed command writes nothing, so it can be run again, and no update is
lost: only the command that holds the lock deletes it. A skill runs the commands one after another.
See [A command fails with a locked queue](troubleshooting.md#a-command-fails-with-a-locked-queue).

### A failed PaceLine hold does not stop the command

When PaceLine cannot take a hold at `stint start`, Stint prints `stint: PaceLine hold not taken:
<why>` on stderr and starts the item anyway. A hold it cannot release is reported as `PaceLine hold
not released` and stays on the item, so a later `stint done` or `stint defer` tries again; otherwise
PaceLine's lease ends it after 240 minutes. The item's state change is kept either way.

**What you see:** an item that runs without a hold is not counted by PaceLine's advice, which may
then offer more budget than is left.

**What still works:** the queue itself: `stint done` and `stint defer` still finish the item.
`paceline hold list` shows the holds that exist.
